'''''Rubia agostinhoi''''' is a climbing plant species of the [[Rubiaceae]] family [[endemic]] to the [[Azores]]<ref name=Catalogue /> It was described by ecologists [[Pierre Dansereau]] and  [[António Rodrigo Pinto da Silva|Pinto da Silva]] in 1977.<ref name="APD">{{cite web |last1=Conservatoire Et Jardin Botaniques Ville De Geneve |title=African Plant Database |url=http://www.ville-ge.ch/musinfo/bd/cjb/africa/details.php?langue=an&id=181201 |accessdate=9 March 2020 |ref=2}}</ref>

==Description==
''Rubia agostinhoi'' has branched, glabrous, brushed or smooth stems, up to {{convert|3|m|ft}} long. It has narrowly elliptical to linear or oblanceolate leathery, dark green leaves with very small, slightly revolted spines in the margins. Leaves of the side shoots are shorter and smaller in length than those of the main stem. Flower stems are {{convert|1|-|6|cm|in}} long and usually very flowery. Fruits are {{convert|5|-|10|mm|in}}, globose and shiny black when ripe.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rubia agostinhoi Dans. & P. Silva |url=http://www3.uma.pt/biopolis/planta.php?id=239 |website=www3.uma.pt |access-date=30 November 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is present in all of the [[Azorean]] islands, except [[Graciosa]]. It is commonly found in ravines, craters, natural forests and heather bushes. From sea level to altitudes above {{convert|1000|m|ft}}.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rubia agostinhoi Dans. & P.Silva |url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/0tQSK |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=30 November 2020}}</ref>
